_note: Normative MUST or MUST NOT clauses verified by schema checks, unit tests, or static validation rather than runtime conformance fixtures. Enforced by scripts/check-coverage.mjs.

exempt.reason: A default-value clause: it fixes what a document without `stream` means, and every content-anchor fixture without `stream` exercises that default implicitly. The rejection path for the one value a fixture can distinguish is fixtured (stream-chunk-unsupported-rejected, [OAR-OPS-6]). A fixture asserting the default itself would have to observe the engine's internal evaluation mode, which the fixture contract has no key for.

An informational-field clause: `emit` is provenance metadata an engine MUST accept and MUST NOT interpret. Acceptance is enforced by the published schema (oar.schema.json) and by every fixture, whose rules carry `emit` and resolve normally; non-interpretation is a negative requirement on engine internals that no single fixture can isolate, because a fixture asserts outcomes, and an engine that ignored `emit` and one that read it produce the same outcomes on every fixture that does not depend on the difference.
exempt.check: spec/oar/1.0/schemas/oar.schema.json, packages/oar-ref/src/load.ts (emit parsed and never read)

exempt.reason: An informational-field clause: `category`, `context_schema`, `scenarios`, and `evidence` are publisher metadata an engine MUST accept and MUST NOT derive behaviour from. Acceptance is enforced by the published schema; non-derivation is a negative requirement on engine internals, and a fixture cannot distinguish an engine that ignores the fields from one that reads them without a fixture whose outcome depends on them — which would contradict the clause.

A negative requirement on selector semantics: an engine MUST NOT match selector clauses against natural-language text or infer values from prose shape. A fixture can only assert what an engine does, not what it refrains from doing internally; every selector fixture asserts the machine-observable matching that is required, and the closed selector-clause vocabulary is enforced by the published schema and the loader.
exempt.check: spec/oar/1.0/schemas/oar.schema.json, packages/oar-ref/src/load.ts (readSelector closes the clause set)

exempt.reason: A normative stance on fact providers: a fact is an observation, never a verdict. It binds providers, not the evaluating engine, and no fixture can observe the provenance of a value — the detector fixture fact-detector-reports-observations-rule-owns-threshold exercises the division of labour the clause states, with the threshold in the rule.

A guarantee of the frozen condition language: the language of section 5 has no assignment, no effectful call, and no input or output construct, so a condition cannot mutate state or perform I/O by construction. The closed grammar is enforced by the parser and the loader's type check; a fixture cannot assert the absence of a construct the language does not offer.

A structural requirement on the engine's declared fact environment: every fact carries exactly one tier. The tiers are fixed in the reference environment (the core and standard tables of section 5) and for host facts by the loader, which assigns tier `host` to every name declared through the host-fact declaration; a fixture observes facts, not the tier metadata behind them.
exempt.check: packages/oar-ref/src/env.ts (tier on every declaration), packages/oar-ref/src/env.ts (withHostFacts assigns tier host), packages/oar-ref/test/env.test.ts

exempt.reason: A completeness claim on the engine's fact environment: an engine MUST provide every core fact of section 5.2. The reference environment declares the full core table, and the corpus exercises the core facts throughout; a fixture cannot assert the presence of a fact no rule references, and a rule referencing all of them at once would test the environment, not the engine's behaviour at an occurrence.

A completeness claim on standard profiles, symmetric with [OAR-FACT-12]: an engine claiming a profile MUST provide all of its facts and functions. The reference environment declares the full content-safety and mcp tables of section 5.4; the corpus exercises profile facts through the detector fixtures. A fixture cannot assert the completeness of a bundle, only the behaviour of the members a rule names.

A negative requirement on the engine's declared environment: an engine MUST NOT redefine the name, type, or meaning of a core or standard fact. The reference environment is a single immutable table; the host-fact loader rejects a declaration colliding with any declared fact or function name, which is the one path a redefinition could take at load.

A digest-stability requirement: `tool_args_fingerprint` MUST be stable across sessions for the same tool and arguments and differ otherwise. Stability is a property over many occurrences and sessions; a single-occurrence fixture can observe one value but cannot assert equality or inequality it has no second occurrence to compare against, and the fixture contract has no cross-fixture state.

A within-occurrence consistency requirement: every rule at one occurrence observes the same value for the same fact. The engine assembles the fact map once per occurrence and passes the same map to every rule's evaluation, so the property holds by construction; a fixture would need two rules observing the same fact and disagreeing to violate it, which the frozen evaluation algorithm cannot express.
exempt.check: packages/oar-ref/src/decide.ts (facts assembled once per occurrence, shared by every rule)

exempt.reason: A permissive clause: a host MAY accept host-native `on` values. The reference engine models only the core anchor set and exercises the rejection path (prof-core-anchor-unsupported-rejected); the acceptance path is host-optional behaviour, and a fixture requiring it would demand capability the specification deliberately leaves optional.

A SHOULD-level tooling clause: an engine SHOULD offer a portability report. It describes an operator-facing feature outside the evaluation and fixture contracts; no fixture key can assert the presence of a report, and the clause explicitly forbids making non-portability a load failure, which the loader observes.

A load-error reporting clause for hints: an engine MUST report a load error in a hint and MUST NOT render a hint that failed to load. The fixture contract asserts one outcome per fixture; a fixture carrying a broken hint alongside a working rule would need a key asserting the hint-level error without failing the whole fixture, which `expected` does not offer. The rejection paths are exercised by the hint fixtures that assert the load error as the fixture's outcome (hint-evaluation-field-rejected, hint-without-copy-rejected, hint-copy-must-be-static), and the loader refuses to register a hint that failed to load.

A requirement on the shape of a fixture, not on engine behaviour: a fixture cannot assert something about its own members. Enforced instead by scripts/check-coverage.mjs, which fails when a fixture's id does not equal its file name stem, when it cites a clause the specification does not define, or when it is not listed in manifest.json, and by the unit test 'every fixture validates against the published fixture schema' in packages/oar-ref/test/corpus.test.ts, which enforces the required members and the closed input and expected vocabularies.

A requirement on the shape of a fixture: the id MUST equal the file name stem and `covers` MUST be non-empty and defined. A fixture asserting this would have to be about some other fixture. Enforced by scripts/check-coverage.mjs, which fails on a stem mismatch and on a covers entry the specification does not define.

A requirement on the shape of a fixture's expected block: the six keys and the rejection of any other key. Enforced by the unit test 'every fixture validates against the published fixture schema' in packages/oar-ref/test/corpus.test.ts, which closes `expected` to its six members, and by the runner, which rejects an unknown expected key rather than passing it silently.

A requirement on the act of claiming conformance: an implementation MUST pass every fixture within its declared profiles and report what it skipped. It binds the implementer's claim, not the engine at an occurrence; the reference runner's report (fixtures passed, clauses exercised) is the reporting mechanism, and no fixture can assert a property of the run that contains it.

A requirement on the shape of the published corpus: every fixture MUST use core anchors and core- or standard-tier facts only. A fixture asserting it would have to be about the corpus rather than an occurrence. Enforced by scripts/check-coverage.mjs and by review of the corpus; the host-fact fixtures declare their host facts through input.host_facts precisely so that the fixture itself remains runnable by an implementation that models no host-specific state.

A versioning-policy clause binding future revisions of the specification, not engine behaviour at an occurrence: a minor revision MUST be additive. No fixture can exercise a revision that has not been published; the policy is enforced by review of each revision against the change log (Appendix A) and by the schema version gate, which pins documents to the major they declare.

A versioning-policy clause binding future revisions: a breaking change MUST bump the major version. Like [OAR-DOC-26] it constrains how the specification may evolve, not how an engine evaluates an occurrence; the major-version gate (doc-unsupported-major-rejected) is the enforceable edge and is fixtured.

A publication-policy clause: a published version is immutable and corrections ship as new versions. It binds the specification's own release process; there is no engine behaviour to fixture, and the version gate plus the change log are the mechanisms that keep published versions distinct.
